segments.text: Question 29. You hear a pharmacist talking to a doctor about a patient's medication. Now read the question.
Sorry to bother you, Dr Baker. I just wanted a quick word about Mrs Milton's prescription,
the one for anti-inflammatories that you gave her after last week's consultation.
Oh yes, for her osteoarthritis.
Yes, so she's been on them for a week now, 500mg twice daily.
The thing is, she's just been into the pharmacy complaining of a headache ever since she started the medication.
Really? Well, that does happen in some patients, but maybe switching her on to a different anti-inflammatory wouldn't be a bad idea.
OK, I'll look into some options and then run them past you later, shall I?
Fine, thanks.
Question 30.
You hear a surgeon talking to a member of his team as they are finishing a surgical procedure.
Now read the question.
Good, there's no more bleeding. The procedure's finished.
Can we just do the sign-out? How much contrast did we use?
That was 120 mils of OmniPake.
And we did reach a high dose, so we'll have to fill out a high dose form.
I'll do that afterwards.
The other thing was that the ultrasound machine was giving us a few problems.
Mmm, yeah. I'll have to get the technician on the phone.
Do it now, though, because we'll need it if we're going to get through all our lists today.
Do we need to send this patient up to HDU?
Actually, everything was quite straightforward, so I'd say a regular ward bed is fine.
That is the end of part B.
Now look at part C.
